description: Path B scaffold step 1: extract the structural h⁶ coefficient of the Borromean Markov trace closed form, and solve for the C_6 required to close each anchor's Higgs residual with the augmented formula m_H = m_anchor · (P/P) · (6/5) · (1 - h⁴·2G - h⁶·C_6). Confirms PR #1167's negative finding that no single C_6 closes both anchors, and identifies the research-grade ~1 month CBH expansion needed for full closure.
next_step: Full Path B step 2: implement the 64-cell tessellation of the Borromean rings complement via Riemann-product subdivision; compute the per-cell CBH expansion to h⁶; sum the cross-cell contributions; verify against the Markov trace closed form. References: arXiv:1007.1250v4 (Yekutieli); existing k=1 scaffold in yekutieli_mi_h2_extraction.py.
structural_lower_bound_on_residual: The W/Z anchor asymmetry (~1.1%) is the LOWER BOUND on what any h^k augmentation can close. The asymmetry is electroweak-mixing (cos θ_W), not an h-order phenomenon. Per items 5, 6, and 1 of this session's deferred-list closure, all simple structural augmentations (Q_m, ⋈_K Q-projection, H_4↔H_2 bridge) have been ruled out. Closure to <0.1% requires substrate-derivation of v (Path A, policy-declined) or the full Yekutieli MI k=3 CBH expansion (Path B, research-grade).
verdict: Single C_6 FAILS to close both anchors (confirms PR #1167). Required C_6 differs by -134.1543 between W and Z. The structural Borromean Markov h⁶ = -1/16 does not match either anchor. Full Path B closure requires the 64-cell CBH expansion (research-grade ~1 month) to capture cross-cell h⁶ contributions beyond the bare Borromean term.
